groups.title: Rendered on the server
groups.text: A PAD custom tag writes the custom element with its shadow root already in it - declarative shadow DOM - so it shows, styled and slotted, before any script ran.

groups.title: Upgraded in the browser
groups.text: A small module defines the element: it finds the root PAD rendered and adds behaviour - keys, clicks, a post back, a value in a form.

examples.title: Cards with slots
examples.lede: {card title='Revenue'} is a PAD custom tag that writes <pad-card> with its shadow root: encapsulated styles inlined by {shadow css=}, named slots the browser fills from the light DOM - and not a line of JavaScript.

examples.title: Tabs, upgraded
examples.lede: The tabs are complete HTML when they arrive - the first panel shows. Once tabs.js defines <pad-tabs>, the element takes the root PAD rendered and adds clicks and arrow keys.

examples.title: A rating that posts
examples.lede: <pad-rating value="4"> gets its value from PAD and its stars from the server; a click posts the new rating with the session's CSRF token, and the element shows the average PAD answers.

examples.title: A field of a form
examples.lede: <pad-stepper> is form-associated: ElementInternals gives the {form} its value, the post carries it like any field, and padValidate checks it on the server.

examples.title: A library: Lit
examples.lede: A Lit element rendered in the browser, fed by PAD through an attribute: items="{^items}" is JSON Lit reads into a property - the same data any element gets.
